notes: Alignment was by sentence in the source text. Main disagreements: (1) phase, where coders split on before-course versus during-work or course-start for institutional set-up duties and user duties, and on when-misuse versus during-work for definitions of prohibited conduct; resolved by asking whether the passage concerns institutional/course design, communicating expectations, or what a user does while working. (2) modality, mostly must versus should or informs for unhedged imperatives and for statements of rights or assumptions; resolved by the source wording (an unhedged imperative or 'must' is must, 'should' is should, a right or assumption is may or informs). (3) policy_type, where incident and reporting duties (coder A P50) and automated-decision limits (coder B P46) were sent to UNCOVERED by constant comparison, scope sentences went to P61, and nondisclosure/learning-objective rows went to P28 and P32. (4) unit_stance on duties such as verification, copyright and disclosure where one coder used require or restrict; verification and legal-compliance duties set neutral. Units found by one coder were mostly real sentences the other skipped or merged. Dropped: two repeats in the AI hub (public-tools restatement; responsibility restatement), and 11 coder-B units in the academic honesty policy that mention no AI (or repeat an already coded sentence). All other one-coder units were kept.
